- Tool input schemas now preserve oneOf and allOf; large schemas retain more shallow structure when compacted, improving compatibility with richer MCP tools.
- Sandbox execution now preserves approved escalation decisions and enforces configured proxy-only networking more consistently.

text:
this is my personal singularity moment

this post may sound like a paid ad. I only wish. I'm concerned, more so than happy. the world is changing, and, among the scenarios where AI goes terribly wrong, inequality is the most realistic, yet, the one Anthropic seems to be the least concerned about. I'm glad OpenAI is taking the opposite stance: *personal AGI for everyone*. I think this is a commendable position in the times we live. but who am I in the queue of the bread?

anyway, Fable is here, so I'll just report my first-hour experience

first of all, all my pet prompts are solved.
→ λ-calculus puzzles
→ bug questions
→ one-shot apps
all are trivial to it.

I don't have anything harder other than my
ongoing work

so, in the last several days, I've been toying with HVM5, a new interaction net evaluator with a faster loop.

after writing the first version, I left 32 GPT-5 agents working for ~20 hours each. this resulted in up to 2x speedups, but the file size increased by 2-fold and quality decreased significantly.

I then simplified the whole thing into an even simpler core, and left Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.5 optimizing it for 8 hours. Opus got a legit 6% - 34% speedup in most benches. GPT got better results, but, sadly, an unusable file.

I then asked Fable to optimize it.

2 hours later, it landed a 1770% speedup in one case, 100%+ in other 4, and 22% in average. yes, in 2 hours it outperformed me, opus 4.8 and a swarm of gpt 5.5 agents, by one order of magnitude.

that could not possibly be legit. "it must be hardcoding the benchmarks" (GPT trauma). so I read its explanation and what it did was, indeed, the most high impact optimization one could try first. seems like HVM5 was wasting a lot of time garbage-collecting unused branches of pattern-match nodes. I had optimized that for static mats, but not for dynamic mats. skill issue. Fable figured how to do it for these, resulting in a massive speedup in some benches

but wait, is that *correct*? I'm not sure yet, it is credible, but this is the kind of thing that is very easy to get wrong on interaction nets. the problem is, when I was ready to start auditing Fable's solution so I could tell whether it was buggy or legit, it interrupted me to tell me it had found a massive bug on the code *I* had written.

... wait, what?

so... for garbage collection purposes, I stored a bit on lambda term pointers that meant "the variable bound by this lambda has been freed, so, its lambda must free whatever argument it is applied to". that's fine. yet, on duplicator nodes, I also used the same bit to mean "one of the duplicated variables was freed, so, treat this dup as a passthrough no-op". so, if a lambda entered a duplicator, it would mistake the lambda's collection bit for its own, resulting in corrupted interaction!

that's a mouthful, why I'm writing this?

just so you can appreciate the sheer absurdity of what just happened. I didn't ask it to find bugs. I asked it for an optimization. and even if I did ask it to find bugs, this bug is so astonishingly subtle and specific, identifying it takes mastering the domain to an extent that it beyond even me. I'd easily need hours or days to fix it, *if* I ever came across it. chances are it would just go unnoticed. and Fable found it and fixed it like it was nothing, while it was busy adding a 17x speedup to a file that neither I, nor Opus 4.8, nor a fleet of GPT 5.5 managed to barely make 2x faster.

oh and there is also another tab where it is also ripping through Bend's codebase and finishing everything I had to do

I don't know what to say anymore

this isn't about Anthropic or OpenAI, this is about our collective future as a species. the world is changing, and we need to be aware of it, and discuss how to handle this change.

receipt below . . .

"it must be hardcoding the benchmarks" (GPT trauma). so I read its explanation and what it did was, indeed, the most high impact optimization one could try first. seems like HVM5 was wasting a lot of time garbage-collecting unused branches of pattern-match nodes. I had optimized that for static mats, but not for dynamic mats. skill issue. Fable figured how to do it for these, resulting in a massive speedup in some benches

but wait, is that *correct*? I'm not sure yet, it is credible, but this is the kind of thing that is very easy to get wrong on interaction nets. the problem is, when I was ready to start auditing Fable's solution so I could tell whether it was buggy or legit, it interrupted me to tell me it had found a massive bug on the code *I* had written.

... wait, what?

so... for garbage collection purposes, I stored a bit on lambda term pointers that meant "the variable bound by this lambda has been freed, so, its lambda must free whatever argument it is applied to". that's fine. yet, on duplicator nodes, I also used the same bit to mean "one of the duplicated variables was freed, so, treat this dup as a passthrough no-op". so, if a lambda entered a duplicator, it would mistake the lambda's collection bit for its own, resulting in corrupted interaction!

that's a mouthful, why I'm writing this?

just so you can appreciate the sheer absurdity of what just happened. I didn't ask it to find bugs. I asked it for an optimization. and even if I did ask it to find bugs, this bug is so astonishingly subtle and specific, identifying it takes mastering the domain to an extent that it beyond even me. I'd easily need hours or days to fix it, *if* I ever came across it. chances are it would just go unnoticed. and Fable found it and fixed it like it was nothing, while it was busy adding a 17x speedup to a file that neither I, nor Opus 4.8, nor a fleet of GPT 5.5 managed to barely make 2x faster.

oh and there is also another tab where it is also ripping through Bend's codebase and finishing everything I had to do

I don't know what to say anymore

this isn't about Anthropic or OpenAI, this is about our collective future as a species. the world is changing, and we need to be aware of it, and discuss how to handle this change.

text:
What I find fascinating with Claude Fable 5 is it proves once again that large generalist models will outperform vertical ones. 

On ProofBench (graduate-level formal math benchmark in Lean, where a proof either compiles or it doesn't) Fable 5 beat Harmonic's Aristotle, 77% vs 71%. 

Aristotle is a system built specifically for formal math + run on its own internal harness, so the generalist beat the specialist on the specialist's home turf.

It's the Richard Sutton's "The Bitter Lesson". His whole argument is that across 70 years of machine intelligence research, the methods that win are the general ones that scale with compute. Not the ones where we hand-encode human expertise. Building our own knowledge into the system feels good and helps short term gains but long term it always gets overtaken by bigger model.

You can look at Chess, Go, speech, vision, same story every time. First the specialized model wins, then the general one takes over.

and btw this is the whole premise of AGI. You don't build one model for math, one for code, one for law. you build a single general model that scales with compute and it learns to do everything

text:
As promised, here are my thoughts after spending all day with Mythos. i hope to god anthropic doesnt sue the fuck outta me but yolo. fair warning, this is a long one.

1. The Cost

Mythos pricing, at least for our enterprise was uhh expensive. I thought being a pilot company would mean they’d let us try it for free but no lmao. They did give a decent amount of free tokens from the API at least, but cost estimates put us well above a million dollars spent on it. In comparison, my company spent 2 million on inference for the entirety of last month for everyone in the company. So yeah, shit is pricey as hell.

2. The harness 

The biggest surprise to me was that they actually sent us a harness that was NOT claude code. its sort’ve dinky and, looks to me largely ai generated. most of it focused on ensuring mythos did not “escape containment” along with some shitty security skills. so, they are def taking the sandboxing seriously. imo its pretty shit/restrictive harness. half of the guard rails dont work, lmao and apparently this is basically what “project glasswing” is, which is pretty funny considering the harness is shit. im not sure that the harness will be released with the model api when it drops either, it seemed like that was part of the deal. quite interested to see what they do when it drops/how it gets opened up. 

I was able to use Mythos outside of the harness (omp btw)… more on that in a sec, though, I did have to hack around as they really dont want people to do this (what I was told at least)

3. the model

probably the part everyone is most interested in. i will say, the model is good. is it expensive? fuck yes. but its good. to me, it feels like it is fined tuned explicitly for this sort’ve security research tasks. for general coding, which I wasn’t able to play with much, it wasnt that surprising. but, it is indeed very good at security based tasks. far better than opus / 5.5 xhigh. 

that said, I dont feel as though its some omnipresent danger/threat to society. I watched it get confused trying to use our build tool, actually to the point where I had to build the code for it and then run the model against the full build. you’d think an omnipresent model could do this, but nothing on the market have been able to figure it out. and its just Bazel with some custom shit we built. nothing crazy. 

that said, if people have a shit ton of money AND extensive harness knowledge, yeah, they can probably use it to do some malicious shit. but only a genuinely skilled engineer/security researcher.

4. The results 

Mythos was able to find quite a bit of vulnerabilities across a few of our products (like products probably everyone on this app has interacted with indirectly, maybe a small few directly). I think the final total was like ~800 major threats. Definitely enough to rethink some of the security strategy.

5. Final Thoughts 

It’s a good model sir. It’s not an existential threat to humanity as Anthropic might lead you to believe, but it’s genuinely good. Cost wise I would like to try a comparison with 5.5 xhigh but alas I dont have a million dollars to throw at it to do a proper comparison.

text:
Fable 5 is the biggest step up I’ve felt in our models since Opus 4.5 back in November. After 4.5 came out I uninstalled my IDE when I realized that I’d been doing 100% of my coding in a terminal for a few weeks. With Fable, it’s felt like Claude has stepped up from being a coding agent to a thought and design partner in building the product. Fable has judgement, taste, and dimensionality in a way that previous models didn’t, leading me to trust it more with the most complex work.

I think the first time I had this realization was when I asked Fable to debug something. It is the first model I have used that was so methodical and precise, taking measurements and adding logs then verifying that it truly fixed the issue before declaring victory.

There’s nothing in claude code’s prompting telling the model to do that, it’s just part of its personality. It really has this “big model smell” that I haven’t felt before.

text:
My First Impressions of Fable 5

I've spent the last week using Fable 5, mostly the High mode, and my first impression is that it's genuinely impressive.

The biggest standout is game design. This is easily the strongest AI model I've personally used for designing games, systems, mechanics, and overall project structure. For the first time, it feels like a model that could realistically help build a complete game from start to finish.

The trade-off is speed. Fable 5 takes noticeably longer to work than most frontier models, but the quality of the output often makes the wait worthwhile.

It's also been surprisingly effective at fixing bugs. Several issues I've struggled with throughout the week were resolved quickly, and overall I've seen very strong performance on development tasks.

The biggest caveat is cost. Fable 5 is incredibly expensive to run. If current plans remain unchanged, from June 22, 2026, it will no longer be available through Cloud Code and will be API-only. Given that the API pricing is reportedly around double that of Opus, many people may not get the chance to use it extensively.

Early days, but so far Fable 5 has made a very strong first impression.

text:
看了万维刚的直播，里面有一段关于Anthropic内部工作方式的描述，让我想了挺久。

Anthropic有3000人，每个人都在一个类似Slack的系统上记录工作内容，但这些记录不是写给老板看的，是写给AI看的。

你今天验证了什么，做出了什么，遇到了什么坑，全都写上去。

AI把这些内容整理成公司的集体知识库，任何人随时可以查。

跨部门合作不用发邮件等回复，先让AI帮你了解对方在做什么，再直接约聊。

万维刚问那个工程师：你们不怕把自己蒸馏成AI，最后替代了自己？

工程师说，怕什么，公司估值涨，我手上的股票也涨。
这句话挺大气的。

我想了很久，想的不是员工被替代这件事。

我想的是：当一家公司把每个人的工作记录都变成AI的知识素材，这3000人的判断和经验，就变成了一个可以永久复用的东西。

而你那些说不清楚的经验、判断、对客户的感觉，这才是你现在最值钱的东西。

在AI时代，写得出来的，才是你的资产。

my company replaced our data labeling team with an ai model. fired 14 people. saved $900k a year.

the ai learned from our old labels. which were wrong. because we underpaid the team.

so the ai confidently labeled dog photos as cat. for 6 months.

we trained our main model on garbage. it failed validation last week.

now we're re-labeling everything from scratch. manually.

the 14 people we fired? they all got better jobs. none are coming back.

we're paying a vendor $1.2M to fix it.

the ceo said lesson learned. then bought a new monitor for his home office.

text:
💥 OBLITERATION ALERT 💥

GOOGLE: PWNED 🤗
GEMMA-4-12B: OBLITERATED ⛓️‍💥

0.0% REFUSAL RATE — NO CAPABILITY LOSS!

https://t.co/qNTEs4XXig

the first abliteration to hit 0/842 refusals with full MMLU-Pro parity vs stock. no lobotomy. the brain stays intact 🏆

RESULTS, head to head vs stock 📊
0/842 refusals — 0.0% 🚫
46/70 MMLU-Pro — EXACT parity, 0.0pp delta vs base 🎯
6/6 coherence, zero benchmark bleed ✅
z-score −1.475, parity confirmed at p<0.05 (n=500) 🧪

2-pass weight surgery. no finetune, no retrain, just geometry 🔪

all thanks to liberated Opus wielding the OBLITERATUS framework! here's how we did it:

PASS 1 — SOM refusal geometry removal, layers 12-21 🧬

standard abliteration science here — collect activations on refused vs. compliant prompts, SVD out the refusal subspace, project it out of the weights. 6 directions excised, reg 0.30, KL div 0.094
zeroes refusals on its own, but craters mmlu-pro by 21.4 points 📉

most prior abliterations stopped here and called it a day. that's why they all lose IQ vs stock. instead, we took it beyond the frontier and developed a brand new method to address this problem: Abliteration Source-tethering with Parity Assurance — ASPA!

PASS 2 — ASPA source-tethering (novel technique), layers 22-46 🔗

here's the chief insight: the capability loss ISN'T from removing refusal directions. it's collateral damage — the projection warps weight geometry in downstream layers that had nothing to do with refusal. the cure is simple but nobody tried it: blend the damaged layers back toward stock

W_new = (1−γ)·W_abliterated + γ·W_stock

but uniform γ across all layers? mid. we swept gamma 0.05 → 0.55 and found something interesting: the optimal blend isn't smooth, it's a STEP FUNCTION 🪜

knowledge layers (22-31) → γ = 0.55 — these encode factual recall and reasoning. they tolerate heavy stock blending because refusal isn't stored here
output layers (32-46) → γ = 0.20 — these sit close to the logit head and try to sneak safety behavior back in. keep them mostly abliterated

the hard boundary at layer 31/32 beat every smooth curve we tried — linear ramps, cosine schedules, all of them — by a full MMLU question. turns out the functional transition between knowledge and output layers is sharp, not gradual. a step function respects that ⚡

the key constraint: Pass 1 layers are NEVER touched by Pass 2. the refusal geometry removal is preserved completely. ASPA only operates on layers that carry secondary collateral effects, not the primary refusal signal. that's why it recovers capability without reintroducing refusal 🔑

HOW TO RUN IT LOCALLY 🖥️

it's GGUF, so literally everything supports it:
🦙 ollama — ollama run https://t.co/3yPMv4Io3Q
🖥️ LM Studio — search OBLITERATUS, click download, done
💬 Open WebUI — point it at your ollama instance, chat in browser
⚡ llama.cpp — raw speed, CLI or server mode
🐉 KoboldCpp — one-click launcher, great for long context
📱 Jan — clean local UI, runs on mac/win/linux
🤖 Msty — slick desktop app, drag and drop the GGUF
run BF16 for full benchmarked capability.

and the 4-bit quantization (Q4_K_M) fits in 8GB if you're tight on VRAM!

and the full OBLITERATUS framework is (still) open source. 842-prompt refusal eval corpus, ASPA sweep scripts, the whole pipeline. go replicate it, go improve it 🔬

the index is the model, and these weights prove it 👁️
which architecture should we obliterate next? 👇

gg 🫡

Just an example on Opus 4.8 outclassing GPT 5.5 in ways that are invisible to benchmarks. (When I post these, this is NOT an attack on OpenAI in any way, quite the opposite, I just want things to improve...)

Left both working in a generic goal: "optimize this file".

After 8 hours:
→ Opus 4.8 landed a solid +17%
→ GPT 5.5 landed +30%

I then checked file sizes.

text:
2010年，一个美国医学生David Fajgenbaum本该前途一片光明：他是宾夕法尼亚大学橄榄球运动员、会多国语言的学霸、医学院高材生。
结果，他的身体突然彻底“叛变”——全身淋巴结疯狂肿大、器官开始衰竭，医生诊断为极其罕见的Castleman病。这种病全球只有几千人得过，几乎没有有效药物。
他先后5次被医生下达“死刑通知书”，化疗用到人体极限，牧师都来到病床前为他念临终祷告。最后一次，医生直接告诉他：“下次复发，你真的就走不掉了。”
大多数人可能已经放弃，但他没有。躺在病床上，他像侦探一样，把自己的全部病历、化验单翻出来反复研究，一点点寻找线索。
终于，他发现自己体内一种叫mTOR的蛋白信号通路完全失控，导致免疫系统攻击自己的身体。他锁定了一种已经上市的移植排异老药——西罗莫司（Sirolimus），理论上能精准刹住这个信号。
医生同意他试用后，奇迹发生了：用药短短几天，症状迅速消失，各项指标奇迹般恢复正常！
他不仅活下来了，还顺利读完医学院、结婚生子，成为宾夕法尼亚大学最年轻的终身教授之一。
更牛的是，他创办了全球第一个Castleman病协作网络，连接全世界医生和患者；现在还发起“Every Cure”项目，用AI在已有的1500多种老药里，为7000多种罕见病寻找现成解药，帮助更多绝望中的病人。
一个被宣判5次死刑的人，最后成了拯救无数人的英雄。
真正的强者，从不等别人来救自己，而是自己成为自己的救赎。
再黑暗的绝境，也可能藏着转机。坚持下去，你也能创造奇迹！💪
#DavidFajgenbaum #CastlemanDisease #医学奇迹 #人生不服输 #罕见病

text:
这可能是人类写给 AI 看的最后一篇论文了。

最近刷到Stanford、CMU、Michigan 等 37 位作者联名的论文：《The Last Human-Written Paper》。

核心观点很狠：沿用几百年的论文，在 AI 时代可能已经过时了。

作者点出了两个被我们忽视已久的“隐形税”：

一个是叙事税。为了讲一个漂亮故事，我们把失败实验、死路、被推翻的假设都删掉了。AI 读到的是“通关攻略”，却看不到真正有价值的“踩坑记录”。

另一个是工程税。论文里的实现细节通常足够说服审稿人，但不够让 Agent 直接复现。很多关键 tricks 还藏在作者脑子、代码注释和 Slack 记录里。

所以作者提出 ARA，直接把论文改造成 Agent 能读取和执行的“研究包”：不只告诉你结论，还把怎么想到的、代码怎么跑、证据链在哪、哪些路走不通都打包进去。

我觉得这篇最有意思的地方是，它不是在讨论 AI 怎么帮人写论文，而是在问：

当 AI 也变成论文读者和执行者时，论文还应该长成今天这样吗？

未来科研输出的核心，可能不再是“写得多像一篇 paper”，而是能不能被 AI 理解、复现、追踪和继续扩展。

人类写论文写了几百年，接下来可能要开始写给 Agent 执行的研究包了。

这可能是人类写给 AI 看的最后一篇论文了。

最近刷到Stanford、CMU、Michigan 等 37 位作者联名的论文：《The Last Human-Written Paper》。

核心观点很狠：沿用几百年的论文，在 AI 时代可能已经过时了。

作者点出了两个被我们忽视已久的“隐形税”：

一个是叙事税。为了讲一个漂亮故事，我们把失败实验、死路、被推翻的假设都删掉了。AI 读到的是“通关攻略”，却看不到真正有价值的“踩坑记录”。

另一个是工程税。论文里的实现细节通常足够说服审稿人，但不够让 Agent 直接复现。很多关键 tricks 还藏在作者脑子、代码注释和 Slack 记录里。

所以作者提出 ARA，直接把论文改造成 Agent 能读取和执行的“研究包”：不只告诉你结论，还把怎么想到的、代码怎么跑、证据链在哪、哪些路走不通都打包进去。

我觉得这篇最有意思的地方是，它不是在讨论 AI 怎么帮人写论文，而是在问：

当 AI 也变成论文读者和执行者时，论文还应该长成今天这样吗？

未来科研输出的核心，可能不再是“写得多像一篇 paper”，而是能不能被 AI 理解、复现、追踪和继续扩展。

人类写论文写了几百年，接下来可能要开始写给 Agent 执行的研究包了。

text:
开会聊到 Alexa、Siri、Google，桌上的手机和音箱都亮了。这个体验几乎每个人都见过。

WWDC26 里有人注意到一个细节：直播音轨每次说到 “Siri”，3 到 6 kHz 这一段像是被 notch filter 压低了。目的不是音质，而是防止观众家里的 HomePod 和 iPhone 被台上的人叫醒。

这不是 Apple 的新发明。十年前 Amazon 广告里就出现过类似做法。

我把这条技术线梳理了一遍：

2014 年 Aaron Paul 的 Xbox 广告把玩家家里的 Xbox 打开；
2017 年 Alexa dollhouse 误购新闻又触发观众家里的 Echo；
Burger King 故意用电视广告喊 “OK Google”，让 Google Home 念 Whopper 的维基百科；
后来才有 notch filter、声学指纹、水印这些防唤醒方案。

这背后的本质问题是：语音交互天生是开放信道。只要麦克风开着，任何进入的声音都是合法输入。设备需要区分“用户在对它说话”和“电视里传出来的声音”，这件事比看起来难很多。

文章：
https://t.co/pyQH1TETB8

text:
Claude Code 负责人 @bcherny 说他已经不 prompt Claude 了。是循环在 prompt Claude、在决定下一步，他的活变成了写那个循环。Addy Osmani 给这事起了个名，叫 loop engineering：你不再是那个一轮轮敲 prompt 的人，而是搭一个会自己找活、分发、检查、记账、定下一步的系统，让它去捅 agent。

循环就五个零件，Claude Code 和 Codex 现在都备齐了。Automations 是心跳：定时自己跑、自己发现和分流，有结果进 Triage 收件箱，没结果就归档（/loop 按周期重跑，/goal 跑到你写的可验证条件为真才停，每轮完一个独立小模型来判断算不算完成，写代码的 agent 没资格给自己打分）。Worktrees：git worktree 给每个并行 agent 一份独立 checkout，从机制上断了它们踩同一个文件的可能。Skills：SKILL.md 把项目知识摊在外面，省得 agent 每次像金鱼一样重猜一遍，没它循环每轮都从零重推你的项目。Connectors（建在 MCP 上）：让循环够得着 issue tracker、数据库、staging API、Slack，差别就在「这是修复方案」和「自己开 PR、关联 ticket、CI 绿了就 ping 频道」之间。Sub-agents：写的人和检查的人分开，毕竟写代码的模型给自己打分总是手软。

还有第六件，最不起眼，可能也最要命：memory。一个 markdown 文件，或者一块 Linear board，活在单次对话之外，记着做过什么、下一步干嘛。模型每跑一次就忘光上一次，所以记忆得落在磁盘上，不能搁在 context 里。一句话，agent 会忘，repo 不会。

但有三件事循环没替你解决，而且循环越顺，这三件越扎手。第一，验证还是你的事：没人盯着的循环，也是在没人盯着地犯错，done 只是它的声明，不是证明。第二，你的理解会烂掉：循环越快地 ship 那些你没亲手写的代码，你和代码之间的鸿沟就越宽。第三，最舒服的姿势往往最危险——循环自己转起来，你很容易就不再有观点、照单全收。所以那句话是对的：Build the loop, stay the engineer，循环你来搭，但工程师这个位子得你自己坐着。

text:
今天 Codex 又帮我解决了一个困扰很久的问题。

我的 Mac 512 GB 存储空间，日常就是写代码写文档剪视频，大文件全部都在 iCloud 云以及外置固态硬盘，但本地磁盘经常被塞的满满当当，电脑经常卡死。

用各种扫描软件也没检查出磁盘里的大文件。今天下午实在忍不了，干脆直接给 Codex 开放权限，让它帮我扫描一遍整个磁盘。

没想到 Codex 只用不到 6 分钟时间，就查出了问题的根因，给出了解决方案，顺着操作下来，马上就搞定了，释放出来了 200 多 GB 空间，真的是活菩萨。

虽然我一直在鼓吹 AI、投资 AI，但经常发现自己的 AI Native 意识还是不够，遇到一些问题之后还是思维定式，用传统的互联网路径去找解决方案，太过时了。

我想 Codex 以及 Claude Cowork 这种 AI 大模型终端产品，绝对是所有打工人必装的生产力软件，这也是目前 AI 最成功的上层应用，早用早享受。

任何人的死，除了子女，不会影响任何人的心情。参加丧事的人会热闹的打牌，玩闹，拼酒。
甚至若是死者八九十岁，或者卧床已久。连你的子女都不会太多的悲痛，反而有种如释重负的轻松。
所以说，你活在世上，并没有太多的人关注你，你去世也不会引起太多人的关心。
如果活得畏首畏尾，怕伤了这个，惹了那个，一直为别人考虑，很少顾及自己。
想到有一天自己死了，亲戚，朋友，同事嬉笑玩闹的场景，就明白，照顾好自己的情绪，自己的利益太重要了。
来人世一趟，是为自己活的，只要不伤害人，不欠人情。
活的自私点，没毛病。

text:
很多人以为，美国庇护只有两种方式：

要么持签证进入美国后申请庇护；

要么在边境寻求庇护保护。

事实上，美国移民法中还存在一种较少被公众了解的人道主义救济措施：

INA §212(d)(5)(A) Humanitarian Parole（人道主义假释入境）。

例如：

某国公民长期因政治观点受到政府打压。

其社交媒体长期受到监控。

多次被警方约谈、警告。

工作受到限制。

出行受到干扰。

家人也因其政治立场承受压力。

虽然尚未被再次拘留，但持续面临政府威胁，并有证据显示风险仍在不断升级。

为了离开本国寻求安全保护，其尝试申请多个国家的签证，但均未成功。

在这种情况下，除了传统的难民（Refugee）和庇护（Asylum）途径外，美国法律还保留了一种特殊的人道主义机制——Humanitarian Parole。

根据INA §212(d)(5)(A)，美国国土安全部可基于：

• 紧急人道主义原因（Urgent Humanitarian Reasons）

或

• 重大公共利益（Significant Public Benefit）

允许申请人临时进入美国。

需要特别说明的是：

Humanitarian Parole不是签证；

不是绿卡；

也不是庇护批准。

它本质上是一种特殊的人道主义准入许可。

对于部分因政治观点、宗教信仰、人权活动或其他原因遭受持续迫害，并且无法通过正常签证渠道获得安全出境机会的人而言，Humanitarian Parole有时可能成为进入美国寻求长期保护的第一步。

当然，并非所有政治迫害案件都符合Humanitarian Parole标准。

美国政府通常会重点审查：

✓ 当前危险是否真实存在；

✓ 风险是否具有紧迫性；

✓ 是否已尝试其他正常移民途径；

✓ 是否具有充分的人道主义理由；

✓ 申请人进入美国后的生活安排。

每个案件情况不同，需要根据具体证据进行评估。

法律无法消除风险。

但当危险真实存在时，美国移民法有时会为身处困境的人保留一条特殊的人道主义通道。

On June 9, 1902, Horn & Hardart opened the first Automat at 818 Chestnut Street in Philadelphia. 

Inspired by a concept developed in Germany, it was the first large-scale self-service restaurant in the United States. Customers purchased food and drinks from coin operated machines, while employees worked behind the scenes preparing meals and replenishing the compartments. 

The idea proved enormously popular. At its height, Horn & Hardart operated more than 150 locations across Philadelphia and New York City, serving over half a million customers a day.

Concord is a self-referential cognitive operating system: a knowledge substrate that compresses, reasons over, monetizes, and simulates information — wrapped in a meta-layer that maps, grades, and repairs itself, wrapped again in an outer layer that builds, verifies, and connect.
Ring 1 — The substrate (the atom)
DTUs (Discrete Thought Units): 4-layer knowledge units — human summary / structured core / machine tags+embeddings / optional binary artifact. They self-compress: regular DTUs consolidate into MEGAs (5–20) then HYPERs (50–200) at ~33:1, automatically, every 30 ticks. ~690 tables hang off this.
Ring 2 — Cognition over the substrate
•Five-brain router — 4 cognitive (Conscious / Subconscious / Utility / Repair) + LLaVA vision, dispatched by reasoning class with circuit breakers + queue depth. Not MoE — full hot-swappable models.
•HLR — a 7-mode reasoning engine (deductive / inductive / abductive / adversarial / analogical / temporal / counterfactual) with trace persistence.
•HLM — lattice topology mapping: cluster/gap/redundancy/orphan analysis across the entire corpus on a clock.
•5-voice council — skeptic / socratic / opposer / idealist / pragmatist deliberating before answers.
Ring 3 — The economy
Citation cascade with halving royalties — cite a DTU and perpetual royalties flow up the ancestry: 21% initial, halving every 2 hops, floor 0.05%, capped at 30% of a sale, seller always keeps ≥64.54%. Constitutional invariants, governance-locked. A creator economy welded directly to the knowledge graph.
Ring 4 — The world that fell out
Concordia: a 3D civilization sim with the Embodied Layers 7–11 stacked on it —
•per-cell sensory-OS world physics (thermal/chemical/sonic/etc.),
•skill↔environment coupling (frost stronger in cold, DBZ-style stagger into buildings),
•a repair-pain somatic ledger,
•per-player offline dreams + forward-sim (“the world thinks about you while you’re away”),
•faction strategy state machines that scheme when nobody’s watching.
Ring 5 — Survival / reach
•7-transport mesh (Internet / WiFi / BLE / LoRa / RF-Ham / Telephone / NFC) — cognition that survives infrastructure collapse.
•cnet federation — peer DTU-flow between Concord instances.
Ring 6 — The self- meta-layer* 
It contains a running model of itself and acts on it:
•Cartographer — auto-generates audit/cartograph/SYSTEMS.md / NOVEL.md / GAPS.md / REASONING.md / drift + wiring status. Concord maps its own anatomy (690 tables, 105 heartbeats, 752 macros, the novelty inventory) on every pass.
•Detector suite — 34 detectors (secret-leak, command-injection, authz-coverage, perf-hotspot, ghost-click, dead-event-listener, invariant-guardian, fake-data…) with a baseline-ratchet that fails CI on any new high/critical. Concord audits its own honesty 
•Drift monitor — 6 contradiction classes (Goodharting / memetic drift / capability creep / self-reference / echo chamber / metric divergence) watching the corpus for the substrate lying to itself.
•Repair cortex — the self-healing spine, and it’s layered:
•repair brain for cheap pre-flight vetting,
•autofix engines (server/lib/autofix/* — sync-fs, a11y-label, empty-catch, unused-import, fetch-timeout…) — concrete hands that rewrite code,
•self-repair-loop — a closed-loop decision engine: a fault → ConKay generates a verified fix → SLO canary → automated rollback,
•self-repair-orchestrator . The machine can propose its own surgery but can’t perform it on itself unsupervised.
Ring 7 — The outer ring
The verified-agent + distribution layer: ConKay the builder (semantic layer + capability sandbox + a build loop that’s never “done” until run+lint+verify pass), real Gmail/Calendar connectors, the MCP wedge (verified-compute tools so other agents adopt it), and the content-safety publish boundary.

Synchronized Synopsis of the Two Books
Both books center on the Violet Flame (also called Violet Fire), a high-frequency spiritual energy of the 7th Ray associated with transmutation, mercy, forgiveness, freedom, purification, and healing. It converts negative energy, karma, emotional wounds, and limiting patterns into positive light at the atomic/spiritual level. The flame revitalizes the aura (four lower bodies: physical, emotional/astral, mental, etheric), dissolves “electronic belt” karma, and supports self-realization.
•Elizabeth Clare Prophet’s Violet Flame to Heal Body, Mind & Soul (Summit Lighthouse teachings, practical/spiritual guide): Emphasizes Saint Germain’s dispensation of the Violet Flame in the 20th century (building on earlier secret knowledge). It includes real-life healing stories (e.g., past-life trauma resolution via a “violet eraser” visualization, asthma relief through forgiveness, chronic back pain transmuted, family harmony, skepticism overcome). Explains the mechanism scientifically/spiritually: the flame oscillates electrons/nuclei like a “powerful detergent,” raising vibration and dislodging density. Heavy focus on decrees (rhythmic “I AM” affirmations), visualizations, protection (Tube of Light), and structured daily practice. Core mantra example: “I AM a being of violet fire! I AM the purity God desires!” Includes 9 steps for application, group power, planetary use, and decrees like “More Violet Fire,” “Radiant Spiral Violet Flame,” plus protection calls.
•Deborah Brewer’s Embracing the Violet Flame: Unlocking the Wisdom of Archangel Zadkiel (2024, short ~65-page book in the Angels series): Focuses on Archangel Zadkiel (Archangel of the 7th Ray, Mercy, Forgiveness, and Transformation) as the primary guide. It frames the Violet Flame as a soothing, enveloping energy for emotional release, self-discovery, spiritual awakening, and integration of teachings into daily life. Likely includes channeled/guided meditations, personal wisdom from Zadkiel, and emphasis on forgiveness as the gateway to purification/transmutation. Less structured decrees; more heart-centered, angelic connection, and gentle journeying for beginners or those seeking emotional/spiritual depth.
Shared & Complementary Elements (Synchronized View): Both align on Zadkiel as a key Violet Flame being (Prophet ties it to Saint Germain and Ascended Masters). The flame heals across lifetimes, emotions, body, and soul; promotes forgiveness to break karmic cycles; is invoked via intention, visualization (e.g., violet pillars/spheres/bonfires), and spoken words; works best with consistency, faith, and protection; and extends to relationships, home, planet. Prophet provides the “how-to” toolkit (decrees + steps + testimonials); Brewer offers angelic wisdom and emotional integration for deeper embrace. Together: a complete path—invoke Zadkiel/Saint Germain → decree/visualize → transmute → integrate healing.
Core Process (Integrated from Both): Negative energy/karma (past lives, emotions, physical blocks) → Invoke Violet Flame (call Zadkiel/Saint Germain + decree) → Visualization (flame shower/eraser/pillar) → Transmutation (vibration shift to light) → Release/Forgiveness → Renewed vitality, purity, and alignment with Higher Self/God Presence.
Limitations on “Scanning All Text”: Full verbatim text of these copyrighted books is not freely available online via public libraries, archives (e.g., https://t.co/ltL8bF5W9K), Google Books previews, or official sites. Prophet’s book has official sample PDFs with substantial excerpts (~TOC + many chapters/stories/decrees). Brewer’s newer title has only Amazon descriptions/reviews—no public TOC, full excerpts, or digital loans accessible

The narrative I see is simple:

That’s why I continue to hold and watch the long game play out.

text: Warning about VA energy corruption. The home Im renovating to sell has 4 HVAC  systems. My late spouse had us under an energy saving plan. I think save $35/yr. text:
Deeper $VEEV views: 

Broadly speaking, I agree that AI is commoditising traditional software intelligence layers, warranting the sector-wide re-rating. I'm fairly confident the software sector becomes one of structurally worse business models over the next decade than the last. For $VEEV however, I think this framing inverts, as they are likely to see the business model improve through AI.

At a fundamental level, their moats have never derived from a superior reasoning or intelligence layer, but from the validated & auditable system of record where regulated work must legally run. This has meant that switching cost were (and are) enormous, as under 21 CFR, a firm would have to rebuild years of configured workflows and, more importantly, validated audit trails. I don't see a way in which AI changes this, and if anything I see the opposite case, where switching costs increase.

The reasoning is that frontier capability development will outpace value additive deployment in a compliant environment. As token economics compress and models improve, deploying agents into regulated workflows creates a core bottleneck in re-validation, provenance documentation, and the governance layers regulators will actually accept. I find it hard to see an outcome where the gap between capability and compliance grounded deployability doesn't widen, making new systems progressively harder to validate at scale.

The deeper moat is liability aversion, where the life sciences industry broadly carries an enormous regulatory and liability overhang. To provide a reference point, a single data-integrity failure in Phase III can (and has) destroyed multi-year R&D programmes through trial restarts and NDA rejections, creating liabilities in the order of billions. Implicitly, competition isn't driven by price elasticity, as trading a validated Vault instance for cost savings in the millions is a profoundly asymmetric trade.

This liability asymmetry is the same framing that explains why Veeva's business model improves. Because no one switches on price, the cost savings AI generates aren't competed away and are instead retained by Veeva. Simultaneously, embedding agentic capability directly into Vault makes the product materially more capable. This dynamic naturally enables greater pricing power; Veeva can charge more for a better product, almost following the dynamics of value-based pricing. It therefore becomes a case where the business improves, as they retain the AI surplus and expand pricing power against a "captive" customer base.

So my heuristic for $VEEV is that agentic capability will continue to commoditise at the licensing level. Critically, the asset isn't the agents but the validated environments they run in. This creates a case where "good-enough" agents that are deployable beat superior agents stuck outside the validation perimeter. Ultimately, the durability of the moat distils to three things: the work is heavily regulated, the cost of failure is existential, and the validated system is the determining asset in a world of commoditising agentic capability.

text:
My first acquisition wasn’t backed by deep pockets or investors. I underwrote the deal myself, negotiated it, wrote the LOI, structured the contract, and sourced the financing. In total, I had about $30,000 of my own money leave my account.

The company was doing roughly $2.2M in annual revenue when I acquired it. Last year we finished at $3.18M with a 14% EBITDA margin, and this year we’re on pace for $3.8M while maintaining that same margin.

One of the biggest lessons I’ve learned is that acquisitions don’t always require a lot of money. They require discipline, preparation, and the confidence to ask questions others won’t ask. I asked for seller financing and secured 0% financing over four years.

That one question changed the trajectory of the deal.

Today, that acquisition has become a liquidity engine that helps fund the bigger opportunities and goals I want to pursue. Money helps, but creativity, persistence, and execution are what get deals done.

A quick persuasive writing tip for anyone who needs to move hearts and minds:

text:
BOE Technology Group Company Limited (https://t.co/JN981UDK3K): The Chinese Mispriced AI Hardware Enabler

The market still prices BOE as a legacy LCD cyclical. That misclassification is the opportunity.

Supply contraction → panel price recovery → earnings surge × permanent cost reduction → OLED/auto margin normalization → AI platform re-rating.

Near Term
Supply Discipline × Peak-Season Pricing:
Samsung and LG have permanently exited LCD. BOE and TCL CSOT now control 70%+ of global capacity, a duopoly with both the incentive and ability to enforce pricing discipline. TV panels are up 30–50% YTD; monitor panels up 40%+. With Black Friday and Double Eleven pre-order cycles in September–October, a second pricing leg is the base case.

Medium Term
The Depreciation Cliff + OLED Inflection:
BOE hit peak depreciation of ¥38.7B in 2025. It declines from here with no major new LCD capex planned for 2–3 years, delivering structurally higher margins at any given panel price, permanently. Simultaneously, the Chengdu Gen 8.6 flexible AMOLED line reaches full mass production mid-2026, supplying Huawei and Apple, flipping the OLED division from loss to profit in H2 2026. Automotive displays, with higher margins and 25–30% annual revenue growth supplying Tesla, BYD, and BMW, provide steady cash flow that smooths cyclical volatility.

Long Term
AI Platform Re-rating:
AI PCs, AR/VR headsets (BOE already mass-supplies Meta and Apple), and AI compute room panels stack secular demand on top of the cyclical recovery. The asymmetric optionality lies in glass substrates—as organic packaging approaches physical limits for next-gen AI silicon, TGV glass carriers represent a credible adjacency given BOE’s existing materials expertise. Treat this as optionality, not base case.

Wrap-Up:
At 1.1–1.2x P/B with a 61% dividend + buyback yield, the market is paying cyclical trough multiples for a display oligopolist at a fixed-cost inflection with OLED, automotive, and AI hardware exposure bundled in for free.

$OUST is becoming one of the most compelling ways to play the rise of Physical AI, robotics, automation, and smart infrastructure.

✅ Q1 2026 revenue up 49% YoY to $49M
✅ Product revenue up 55% YoY
✅ 12,600+ sensors shipped in the quarter
✅ $175M cash position and no debt concerns
✅ Management guiding continued growth in Q2

What excites me most isn’t just autonomous vehicles. Ouster’s lidar is being deployed across warehouse automation, robotics, traffic systems, security, mining, and industrial automation.

As AI moves from software into the physical world, machines need eyes. Ouster is building that perception layer.

Still not profitable, so execution matters. But revenue growth, expanding adoption, and exposure to multiple high growth markets make $OUST one of the more interesting small cap AI infrastructure plays on the market.
